fatalFlaws: Lorenz stability claim is false, verified by simulation: "dt = min(intk::dtMax, intk::dtBase * (1 + intk::rateGain * s) * tickScale) // 0.006 .. 0.015 per tick; dtMax 0.02 keeps Euler stable at rho <= 40". Forward Euler at dt = 0.02 with rho = 38 (the design's own ceiling: rhoWild 30 + heatRho 8) diverges to inf in about 3700 ticks (2.7 s); it already blows up at dt = 0.019 (all four seeds, within 30..200 s) and only survives at dt <= 0.018. The worst real operating point (44.1 kHz, s = 1: tickScale 1.088, dt = 0.0163) survives with excursions to |state| 86 against a true attractor of about 50, so the margin to NaN is about 14%, and `dtBase`/`rateGain`/`dtMax` are listed as tuning knobs ("burble speed calm..hot; dtMax is the Euler stability guard"). The escape `if (!isfinite(x+y+z)) reset(seed)` also zeroes `heat`, `dc`, `slewed`, `out`, so when it fires it lands a slew discontinuity of up to the full hero depth on Time.

Control-rate destinations are stepped once per 32 samples with no intra-tick ramp: inside `if samplesToTick == 0:` the skeleton does `loop.setDecay (clamp (decayKnob + dm.decay, 0, 1.15))`, `blend = clamp (blendKnob + dm.blend, 0, 1) -> equal-power gains`, `strengthGain = dbToGain (clamp (strengthKnobDb + dm.strengthDb, 0, 40))`, applied as constants for the next `run` samples. The 3 ms `ctrlSlew` at a 1.5 kHz tick rate is `1 - exp(-0.667/3)` = 20% of the remaining move per tick, so the hero Follower->Decay route (5 ms attack, up to +0.14 gain) is a staircase at 1.5 kHz on a near-saturated feedback signal. Knob values are also "combined with the mod offset ... per tick", which regresses the template's per-sample gain path (ExampleEngine reads driveSmooth/mixSmooth with getNextValue() per sample).

Macros are unsmoothed and applied per sample: `void setMacros (float agitate01, float timeMod01); // per block` and `timeAgitGain = macroTime * modk::timeRangeOct * depth[agitation][time]` is read directly inside `timeOctForSample`. A host automating Time Mod steps the audio-rate FM depth once per block in one sample: at timeRangeOct 2 with Agitation at a rail, a 0.01 knob step is a 24 cent pitch jump. Violates CLAUDE.md "all continuous parameters go through SmoothedValue" and makes the Time path block-size dependent under automation.

Only heap in the subsystem is sized to the prepared block and indexed by the host block: "`juce::HeapBlock<float> chipRatio` sized `maxBlock` in `prepare()`" then `chipRatio[n+i] = fastExp2 (...)` for `n+i` up to `numSamples`. A host that delivers more samples than `samplesPerBlock` (allowed by the JUCE contract) writes past the end. Design 1's 32-sample scratch arrays cannot have this bug.

The drift test's bound is wrong by 2x and can go red on legitimate behaviour: "At `timeDepthOct = 0.004` oct the RMS pitch wander is 1.6 cents, 3-sigma about 4.8 cents, bounded by tanh at 4.8 cents" versus `DRIFT_CENTS_MAX = 8`. Pitch of a variable-clock delay is 2^(L_read - L_write), so the rail-to-rail bound is 2 * 1200 * 0.004 = 9.6 cents, and the 0.6 Hz wow band can cross the rails within one 3.67 s delay period. The same scenario measures pitch by zero crossings (`freqPrecise`) on a saturated Decay 1.05 loop and asserts a 0.3 cent std, which that measurement cannot resolve on a hissy lo-fi wet path.
scores.notes: What it gets right on my lens: strictly no division and no libm call per sample (`fastExp2` with correct Taylor coefficients, relative error about 1.5e-5; `riseInv`/`fallInv` precomputed; `agitSum * invInterval` at the tick), a persistent `samplesToTick` countdown that makes tick timing block-size independent, double-precision Agitation phase (0.016 Hz at 192 kHz is inc 8e-8, below float epsilon at 1.0), every coefficient from seconds with `tickScale` normalising Lorenz dt, a NaN in `loopEnergy` accidentally contained by `std::min (1, NaN)` returning 1, `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` demanded in every EngineTest loop, and an explicit bypass/Clear statement. State discipline is correctly stated (v1 depths are constants, nothing to stamp, and the moment depths become editable they must be stamped). The `heat` integrator (6 s memory pushing rho by +8) and `x += inject * s * loopSample` are the only long-timescale and audio-coupled mechanisms in either design and are what the plan's "never exactly repeats" milestone actually needs. The relative-onset gate (env > -30 dBFS and > 1.8x a 300 ms baseline, 60 ms refractory) is the better guitar gate. `timefm`'s alias line (700 Hz Agitation point-sampled at 1.5 kHz aliasing to 800 Hz, must be < -40 dB re carrier) is the single best proof in either design that Time is truly audio rate. Weaknesses beyond the fatal list: there is no block-size sweep anywhere (only 44.1k/64 and 96k/512), so the one property the persistent countdown exists for is never measured; `timefm` does not pin Time, and the delay-line FM depth scales with |sin(pi fm tau_k)| per tap (at fm*tau integer the sidebands vanish), so the expected -26..-8 dB band is derived from the wrong model; the Interference output is `x` (parks at +-sqrt(beta(rho-1)) at rest) so it needs a 0.3 Hz DC blocker and every lobe switch is a full-scale 2 oct dive at hero depth; linear energy normalisation (`invEnvRef` = 1/0.25) leaves a -30 dBFS loop at s = 0.13, rho 16, inert; the first-block snap of `log2FsKnob` is unspecified, so transport start glides the clock up from whatever the one-pole held (a start-up chirp the PT verdict already flagged); and tell 5 is unreachable from the v1 UI because Agitation->Time ships at depth 0. `agitk::curve` rounding, `agitateOnTime` as an explicit switch, and the Speed readout following the Sweep Rate precedent are all correct house behaviour.

fatalFlaws: Block-size invariance, the design's headline robustness claim, is broken by its own Agitation API: `return sum / n // block mean, the value control-rate destinations use` in `Agitation::process` is a mean over the SUB-block, and the skeleton says "agit/follower ctl values come from the PREVIOUS block's mean/end". With a host block of 33 the sub-blocks run 32, 1, 31, 2, ..., so the filter sees means over 1-sample windows; the 6.7 requirement that block sizes 1/33/128/2048 "match to 1e-6" fails as written. Also two divisions per sub-block (`sum / n`, `timeModMean = acc / n`) become two divisions per sample at block size 1, which is exactly the plan's risk 6 warning.

The `generative` gate contradicts itself: it runs "Agitate 0.7, ... Agit Speed 0.2 Hz" (a 5 s periodic 3-octave filter sweep) and then asserts "50 Hz RMS envelope, normalised autocorrelation for lags 2..40 s: max < 0.6" and "at least 3 distinct 5 s windows where uiLoopEnergy mean differs by > 0.15". The 5 s Agitation cycle puts a strong peak at lag 5 s by construction, so the check is either a spurious red or, if it passes, it is measuring the LFO rather than the chaos. There is no companion Agitate 0 run isolating Interference.
scores.notes: Wins on the inner loop and on containment, and the claims I could simulate hold: RK2 at dt = 18/1378 = 0.0131 with rho 45 never touched the +-60 clamp in 10 minutes at 44.1 kHz or 192 kHz tick rates (z reaches 79, inside its 0..120 range); `wanderRaw = tanh((y - x) * kIntfWanderScale)` is exactly zero at rest (tail mean 0.0000 at rho 18) so a calm loop gives zero Time offset with no DC blocker; std(y - x) is 6.8 at rho 45 (wander RMS 0.33 after tanh, peaks 0.9) and the zero-crossing rate is 25/s at 18 units/s, matching the stated 20-30 Hz band. `ControlRamp` (increment `* kInvControlBlock`, exactly 32 samples per tick because the countdown is persistent) makes Decay/Absorb/Blend/Strength C0-continuous with no division; `std::array<float, 32>` scratch means no dependence on `samplesPerBlock` at all; macro and Time Mod are smoothed (30 ms, at control rate); the dB energy normalisation (-54..-6) wakes Interference on a -30 dBFS loop; `kAgitMinSegmentMs = 0.5` (sample-rate independent since `minFrac = 0.0005 * speedHz`) prevents a one-sample cliff into Time; the 3.6 bounded-map argument and the predicted 0.5..3 s breathing band are explicit; `gainToDb(NaN)` returns minusInfinityDb so a NaN loop envelope decays `e` to 0 rather than poisoning it; the 6.7 stationarity soak, the 10-minute Lorenz soak at both extreme rates, `demodPitch` (0.1 cent on a lo-fi path), and the square-wave follower test (exact one-pole) are the right measurements. Real defects short of fatal: per-sample `exp2f` is a libm call in the inner loop (fine on arm64, but Design 0's `fastExp2` is the plan-literal answer); no `ScopedNoDenormals` note for EngineTest although `crackleTarget *= crackleDecay` and `crackleEnv` decay into denormals every sample; `snapAll (const Knobs&)` does not include `lSmooth`, so the first block after prepare glides the clock from 0 (a start-up chirp); `struct Applied` uses `ControlRamp` before it is declared; the crackle at up to 400/s and +-0.6 oct in 0.3 ms is a taste risk (and its density at long Time with Decay 0 will be nonzero because pt_1's idle hiss at Time 1.0 is bounded at [-52, -40] dBFS, above `kEnergyFloorDb` -54, which the design itself flags); `kLogFsHardMin = log2(1000)` lets modulation run the clock a third below the plan's 1.5 kHz floor, where the PT voicing curves are saturated and the Time readout and sync clamp would lie; the hysteresis gate (re-arm below -36 dBFS) cannot retrigger on legato; the 400 ms energy release is the only memory, so a steadily hot loop gives stationary chaos with no 5-10 s evolution; the Speed readout "0.02 Hz" rounds 0.016 Hz by 25% and ignores the Sweep Rate precedent (period below 1 Hz); no bypass statement; and tell 5 is unreachable from the v1 UI (Agitation->Time at depth 0) exactly as in Design 0.

graft: Design 0's persistent per-sample accumulator for the Agitation control value: `agitSum += a` per sample across sub-blocks and host blocks, `agitMean = agitSum * invInterval; agitSum = 0` at the tick. Apply the same pattern to Design 1's `timeModMean` and `blockMean` (UI feeds) so there is no `/ n` anywhere in the per-sub-block path; that is what makes the 6.7 bit-match test actually pass at block sizes 1 and 33.

Design 0's `heat` integrator into Design 1's rho: `heat += heatCoeff * (e - heat)` with `kIntfHeatSeconds = 6`, `rho = kIntfRhoMin + e * (kIntfRhoMax - kIntfRhoMin) + kIntfHeatRho * heat` with `kIntfHeatRho = 8`, then `rho = min (rho, 45)`. Keep RK2 and the +-60 state clamps; simulation shows RK2 at rho 45 and dt 0.0131 stays clamp-free for 10 minutes, so the heat term costs nothing in stability.

Design 0's audio coupling into the chaos state: `x += kIntfInject * e * loopSample` with `kIntfInject = 0.15`, `loopSample` = the loop's last post-saturator sample at the tick. Design 1 only feeds the envelope, so its trajectory phase belongs to the clock; the plan's Interference 'IS the audio loop'. Clamp x after the injection like every other update.

Design 0's relative-onset gate detector evaluated per sample inside Design 1's `Agitation::process`: trigger when `env > kGateOnLevel (-30 dBFS)` AND `env > baseline * kOnsetRatio (1.8)` AND refractory == 0 (60 ms), baseline a 300 ms one-pole updated AFTER the test. Keep Design 1's soft retrigger (`phase = lastOut * faEff`) and `kAgitMinSegmentMs`; drop the -36 dBFS re-arm.

Design 0's `timefm` alias-line assertion merged into Design 1's `timemod`: Time pinned at 0.2 (tau 73.2 ms; |sin(pi fm tau_k)| = 0.67/0.96/0.53 for the three taps at 1 kHz), Agitation at fm, assert the sidebands at f0 +- fm AND assert the control-rate alias at (sr/32 - fm) is < -40 dB re carrier. Print the per-tap `2 m |sin(pi fm tau_k)|` factor next to the measured sideband level so a change to N or the fs map is visible instead of a mystery red.

Design 0's chaos triad in the engine tests: (a) second run, same seed, one extra 1e-5 input sample at t = 0, `RMS(a - b) / RMS(a)` over 80..90 s > 0.5; (b) third run, same seed, FNV over 30..90 s equal to run one; (c) two engines without `setSeedsForTests`, FNV differ. Plus the class-level sensitive-dependence check (1e-6 state perturbation: RMS diff < 1e-3 over 0..0.5 s, > 0.3 over 5..10 s).

Design 0's split of the milestone: `generative` at Agitate 0 (only Interference->Time, the drift trim and in-loop noise move anything) carries the non-repeat, pattern-ACF (centroid series lags 2..15 s < 0.8) and FNV-distinct-windows assertions; `generative-agitated` (Agitate 0.6, Speed 0.05 Hz) drops the ACF line and adds centroid std >= 150 Hz. Keep Design 1's breathing check (autocorrelation peak of `e` at lags 0.3..10 s between 0.5 and 5 s) and its energy-ceiling and peak < 0.99 checks on both, and run both at 44.1k/64, 48k/128, 96k/512 as Design 0 does.

Design 0's harness rule: `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` in every EngineTest scenario loop, stated at the top of `EngineTest.cpp`. Design 1's `crackleTarget *= crackleDecay`, `crackleEnv`, the Lorenz ring-down, the drift HP and the follower tail all decay into denormals; offline runs would otherwise be slow and numerically different from the plugin.

Design 0's bypass and Clear statement, verbatim into the engine header: while bypassed the engine keeps running and is fed silence (follower falls, Interference rings down, Agitation keeps its phase); Clear flushes PT buffers and filter states only, never Agitation phase, Lorenz state, drift filters or the Time smoother.

Design 0's drift-under-runaway scenario (220 Hz burst, Decay 1.05, Filter open, Agitate 0, Time Mod 0, only the hidden trim active, 2..40 s) because it is the only test of the telescoping property (pitch = fs(now)/fs(original write), no random walk across passes). Measure it with Design 1's `demodPitch`, set the bound to `2 * 1200 * kDriftTimeOct` (rail to rail), and start from Design 0's `kDriftTimeOct = 0.004` (9.6 cents rail to rail) rather than Design 1's 0.006 (14.4 cents, which is vibrato at long Time). Keep Design 1's Decay 0 `drifttime` single-pass version and its `setDriftDepthForTests(0)` measurement-floor check.

Design 0's `fastExp2` as the per-sample exp2 in `fillTimeRatio` (split x = fi + f, 6th-order polynomial with coefficients 0.6931472, 0.2402265, 0.0555041, 0.0096181, 0.0013333, 0.0001540, exponent bits via memcpy, ~12 flops, no libm) with Design 0's comment 'never go per-block, timefm would fail'. Add a one-line scenario asserting max relative error of fastExp2 against exp2f over [-8, 18] is < 2e-5.

Ramp the Time column's effective depth per sample, not per tick: Design 1 refreshes `effDepth[*][dstTime]` once per tick from the 30 ms control-rate macro one-pole, so an instantaneous Time Mod jump still steps the FM depth by up to 2.2% of 2 oct in one sample when a source sits at its rail. Give the Time column's four `dT[]` gains a `ControlRamp` each (like decay/absorb/blend/strength), set at the tick, `.next()` per sample.

Sanitise the modulation feedback input at the boundary, from Design 1's containment philosophy and the PT verdict's `nan` scenario: `if (!(loopEnv >= 0.0f) || loopEnv > kLoopEnvCeiling) loopEnv = 0.0f` before the dB normalisation (catches NaN and inf without relying on gainToDecibels' accidental NaN behaviour), and on a non-finite Lorenz state reset only x, y, z (never `e`, `heat`, `wanderSlew`), so the worst case is a stuck orbit with continuous output.

Extend Design 1's `snapAll` to the Time path: `lSmooth = lTarget` (and the macro/Time Mod smoothers to their targets) on the first block after `prepare()` and on preset load, coordinated with the PT verdict's `snapTimeOnNextBlock()`, so neither transport start nor a preset change glides the clock in from wherever the one-pole was.

Design 0's Speed readout and range: `logRange (0.016, 1000)` (the infinite_sustainer helper, never `setSkewForCentre`), string function shows the period below 1 Hz ('62.5 s', one decimal), two decimals 1..100 Hz, integers above, unit baked in and parameter label empty, per the Sweep Rate precedent in infinite_sustainer/Source/Parameters.cpp L173-181.

Keep Design 0's `modk::agitateOnTime` (Design 1's `kMacroScalesAllRoutes`) as a single named compile-time switch, and add `kIntfOutputTap` (0 = `y - x` slewed, Design 1; 1 = `x` through a 0.3 Hz DC blocker, Design 0) so the two Interference characters (fast 25 Hz wobble at 0.33 RMS versus slow lobe dives) are one constant apart for the ear pass the plan budgets.
unresolved: Time Mod semantics disagree across the design set, not just between these two: both modulation designs make Time Mod scale the whole Time column (so the Interference->Time hero route is what Time Mod turns up); params.md assumes Time Mod = the Tones sub-oscillator into fs_chip at audio rate (the hardware normal) with Interference->Time under Agitate, and its Wow and Flutter preset relies on that; tests.md assumes Time Mod = Agitation->Time at audio rate after the smoother. This must be decided before ModMatrix, Params and the `timemod` scenario are written; it also decides whether tell 5 is reachable in Phase 3.

Tell 5 (audio-rate ring-mod sidebands) is unreachable from the v1 UI in both designs: Agitation->Time ships at depth 0 and the sub-oscillator is Phase 4. Options: a nonzero hidden Agitation->Time depth so Speed above 100 Hz clangs, or route Agitation into the Time column under Time Mod (tests.md's assumption), or accept the tell as test-only until Tones exists.

Interference energy floor versus the PT core's idle hiss: pt_1's `crust` scenario bounds no-input wet RMS at Time 1.0 to [-52, -40] dBFS, above Design 1's `kEnergyFloorDb = -54`, so at long Time with Decay 0 the crackle density `400 * e^2` is 10..40 ticks/s with nothing playing. That may be the wanted 'ticking/burbling' or a bug; the floor cannot be set until the core is voiced, and Design 0's linear normalisation (envRef 0.25) has the opposite problem (a -30 dBFS loop is inert).

Whether modulation may push fs_chip below the plan's 1.5 kHz floor (Design 1's `kLogFsHardMin = log2(1000)`, 5.5 s delay, 450 Hz reconstruction LPF). The PT designs voice their noise, bit-depth and bleed curves on [1500, 200000] (pt_1 saturates `u` at 1), the Time readout would show a clamped 3.67 s, and Time Sync's 'clamp to 3.6 s max' becomes untrue under modulation.

Whether Agitate scales the Time column (plan-literal 'scales all three', Design 1) or Time Mod is independent so it is never a dead knob at Agitate 0 (Design 0's default). It is the user's call; it changes the Init preset and all four Patch Corner presets in params.md.

Gate mode on sustained or legato sources: the grafted relative-onset detector needs +5 dB over the ring-out; neither design uses infinite_sustainer's HF-band transient detector. A real guitar test decides whether that upgrade lands in Phase 3.

The PT core's behaviour under fast ratio slopes is asserted, not specified, by both designs ('the accumulator is shared so it is continuous'): Design 1's crackle moves the ratio by up to +-0.6 oct in 14 samples, and modulation can reach ratio 4.5 at 44.1 kHz (Design 1 asks the core to tolerate `kMaxRatio = 8`). The loop design must own the interpolation behaviour and the shared ratio ceiling, with a scenario.

Self-start of the generative milestone depends on Phase 1/2 in-loop noise and quantisation levels, not on the modulation system; `SELFSTART_MAX_S = 30` and the -54 dB floor cannot be derived from either design and must be measured once the core is voiced.

Interference character is an ear decision both designs correctly defer: Design 1's `y - x` gives a fast 5..50 Hz wobble (RMS 0.33, verified) and audio-rate static; Design 0's `x` gives slower burble with full-scale lobe dives and a 6 s heat evolution. The `kIntfOutputTap` graft keeps both reachable, but someone has to listen with Decay 1.1 and no input for five minutes.
